chunks: He said: And Hannan ibn Sadir narrated to me

He said: My father was seated, and with him were Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Sayrafi, Abu al-Murahif, and Salim al-Ashl. Abdullah ibn Sulayman said to my father: O Abu al-Fadhl, do you know that a boy was born to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he named him So-and-so, naming him with his own name? Salim said: Indeed, this is true. Abdullah said: Yes. Salim said: By Allah, I prefer that this be true over returning to my family with five hundred dinars, and indeed I am in need of five dirhams to support myself and my family. Abdullah ibn Sulayman asked him: Why is that? He replied: It has reached me in the tradition that Allah presented the status of the Qaim of the Family of Muhammad to Musa ibn Imran. He said: O Allah, make him from the Children of Israel. Allah said to him: There is no way to that. He said: O Allah, make me among his helpers. It was said to him: There is no way to that. He said: O Allah, make him my namesake. It was said to him: You have been granted that.

key_terms.سميي: My namesake / one who shares my name
key_terms.قائم: The Awaited Imam, specifically referring to Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam Musa al-Kadhim being named after Prophet Musa?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological significance of the name 'Musa' for the seventh Imam, linking it to the lineage of Prophet Musa (a.s.) through a divine dialogue. Salim al-Ashl’s preference for this spiritual naming over material wealth underscores the Shia emphasis on *walayah* and the continuity of prophetic identity within the Ahl al-Bayt. The narrative serves as evidence for the Imamate of Musa al-Kadhim, reinforcing the concept of *ism* (naming) as a marker of divine selection and authority.
